title: Redwood Data Retention & PII Controls Demo - PacificTrust Payments
summary: Redwood AE/SE ran a 40-50 minute walkthrough of data handling controls: logging redaction, PII identification, request storage toggles, VPC/private deployment notes, and retention policies. Customer was primarily concerned about retaining minimal request logs for debugging while ensuring PCI/PII tokenization and KMS-managed key controls. Next steps: share SOC2 + KMS docs, propose pilot configuration, schedule bench run in staging.
topics: Overview of Redwood Console settings for request storage
Logging redaction and automated PII detection
KMS / key management & encryption at rest
VPC/Private deployment considerations and audit logs
Demo of Optimize suggestions for reducing retention exposure

Derek to provide sample anonymized payloads for bench run (by 2026-09-21)

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-14
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marco Gutierrez (Redwood Product), Anika Sharma (PacificTrust Head of Security), Derek Holt (Platform Eng), Lena Park (CTO)

Auto-generated summary: quick demo of data retention features, lots of Qs on PII and PCI, next steps to share docs and run bench

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, uh thanks for joining, I know it's a busy week. quick intros, i'm jordan redwood ae, with priya our se and marco on product. how's everyone doin?
[00:08] Lena Park: Good thanks. we just want to see how you handle logs and pii before we commit to any pilot.
[00:12] Jordan Lee: totally, that's today's plan, we'll run through console, api toggles, and some optimize recommendations. Priya will drive the demo.
[00:20] Priya Nair: thanks. i'll share my screen — let me know if the screen share comes through.
[00:25] Derek Holt: yep seeing it.
[00:27] Priya Nair: cool. starting at the Console home — this is the request storage page. top-level control is a per-project toggle: transient only versus persistent storage. transient means request payloads are kept in memory for the lifetime of the request and not persisted to disk; persistent stores keep encrypted records for the configured retention window.
[00:45] Anika Sharma: quick q, by "encrypted" do you mean customer-managed keys? we need KMS separation of duties.
[00:51] Priya Nair: yes, we support both Redwood-managed keys and customer-managed KMS/HSM. you can point to AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or an HSM for on-prem keys when running Private. the console shows the key binding and a note about rotation policies.
[01:05] Jordan Lee: and to add, for Dedicated we can set up a KMS integration and restrict access via RBAC so only ops role can decrypt.
[01:12] Anika Sharma: ok good. we also need to make sure request logs don't capture full card numbers — tokenization or regex redaction?
[01:20] Priya Nair: two layers: first is automatic PII detection — name, email, ssn, credit card patterns — we run a classifier and apply redaction rules. second is configurable regex and schema rules per route, so you can add domain-specific patterns. redaction happens before storage and is reversible only with keys if you choose to persist reversible tokens — otherwise it's irreversible hashing.
[01:45] Derek Holt: so reversible implies you can decrypt? who holds keys?
[01:48] Priya Nair: if you're using customer-managed KMS, you control key access. Redwood never has the plaintext if you choose that mode. reversible tokens are stored encrypted; irreversible is a one-way hash.
[01:58] Lena Park: what's the default? we want safe default.
[02:01] Priya Nair: default is transient storage + automatic irreversible redaction for obvious PII. persistent storage is off by default for new projects.
[02:10] Anika Sharma: great. show us the UI for configuring per-route rules.
[02:13] Priya Nair: sure — under Routes -> Data Handling you can pick a route and toggle "store requests" and then choose redaction: none, automated, custom regex, or tokenization. you can also set retention in days: 0 (delete immediately), 7, 30, 90, or custom.
[02:30] Priya Nair: here's an example: payments/charge route — we set store=false by default, but enable short-term persistent logs for 7 days only for debugging and with tokenization of card numbers.
[02:40] Derek Holt: If we enable for 7 days how do we audit deletions? we need proof for compliance.
[02:45] Priya Nair: audit logs show each deletion job and a checksum of deleted object IDs. you can export audit logs to your SIEM via syslog/s3. We also surface who triggered retention changes via SSO user mapping.
[02:58] Jordan Lee: (interrupting) also note we keep immutable audit entries for config changes — those are metadata only, no payload.
[03:05] Anika Sharma: what about endpoints that call out to 3rd party tools — does redaction happen before any outgoing webhook?
[03:10] Priya Nair: redaction is applied at the request ingress point. you can configure to redact before external calls or to pass through — it's explicit per route for traceability.
[03:20] Lena Park: ok, can we demo the API parameter for toggling storage? like we'll need to flip in infra as part of rollout.
[03:24] Priya Nair: yep — there's an API: POST /v1/routes/:id/config with payload {store_requests: false, retention_days: 0, redaction: "automated"}. i'll paste an example in the chat.
[03:35] [chat paste: link to snippet: https://redwood.example.com/docs/api/retention-snippet]
[03:40] Derek Holt: thanks. latency impact? does redaction in-line add p99?
[03:44] Priya Nair: we benchmarked classifier based redaction and found median added ~3-8ms for simple regex removal, up to 20-35ms for complex ML-based PII classifiers on long payloads. there's an Optimize suggestion to pre-compile regex and apply edge filters to minimize overhead.
[03:59] Marco Gutierrez: also worth calling out caching — if you enable request caching / KV prefix caching, we redaction-apply before caching keys so you don't accidentally cache raw PII.
[04:10] Anika Sharma: good. what about PCI scoped logs — we can't have any PAN anywhere. can you guarantee no persistence?
[04:15] Priya Nair: yes, set store_requests=false for PCI routes and we will not persist payloads anywhere. ephemeral logs for debugging are only kept in memory and discarded post-response in transient mode. if you need to record masked tokens only, tokenization mode will replace PANs with irreversible tokens by default.
[04:34] Derek Holt: on private deployment — we have an air-gapped cluster; how would retention controls surface?
[04:38] Jordan Lee: in Private, the console runs on your control plane and data never leaves your network. redaction rules and retention still apply but keys remain in your KMS / HSM. we can produce an architecture doc for the air-gapped flow.
[04:50] Anika Sharma: please send that.
[04:52] Priya Nair: we'll add the private-run runbook.
[04:55] [06:00] Priya Nair: now i'll show an example of automated pii detection — running a sample payload with a fake card number and an email. you should see the redaction applied in the request preview before it's persisted.
[06:10] [06:15] Priya Nair: (demo) you can see the card is replaced with CARD_TOKEN_xxxx and email is hashed. there's also an audit entry: detected PII type=credit_card confidence=0.92. sometimes the transcription, sorry confidence, shows slightly off — but we log classifier confidence.
[06:32] Anika Sharma: classifier accuracy? we need false negative/false positive numbers for our risk team.
[06:36] Priya Nair: typical provider metrics — we can share evals against our sample corpora: precision ~0.97 for card numbers, recall ~0.95; for names/emails precision is slightly lower. i'll include the eval report.
[06:50] Derek Holt: competitors — i've seen feature X in Anthropic where they only return hash of data. how is your approach different?
[06:55] Jordan Lee: ours is route-level, integrates with KMS for customer-managed decryption, and ties into Optimize to make retention recommendations per workload (e.g., keep 7 days for debug routes with masked tokens).
[07:10] Lena Park: show me the policy UI — we need to enforce retention across teams.
[07:14] Priya Nair: under Org Policies you can set org-wide defaults and enforcement rules. you can pin required settings for PCI scoping: e.g., all routes matching payments.* are forced to store_requests=false and disallow custom redaction overrides.
[07:28] Anika Sharma: nice. what about data subject requests — if a user asks for deletion, how do we handle it?
[07:33] Priya Nair: we have an API to query and delete records by hashed identifier. if you use irreversible hashing we can delete by hash value; if you used reversible tokenization with your keys, you can decrypt and map, then delete. our team can support integrating deletion workflows into your internal tooling.
[07:48] Derek Holt: audit trail needs to show who deleted and proof of deletion. you said checksums earlier?
[07:52] Priya Nair: yep, deletion jobs produce signed audit events and we can ship them to your SIEM or produce an S3 export with signed manifests.
[07:59] Jordan Lee: quick note, deletion manifests include object IDs and the operation timestamp, we can also provide a verifiable HMAC if you want to prove deletion to auditors.
[08:10] Marco Gutierrez: also our Optimize product can spot routes with high risk exposure and recommend reducing retention or applying stricter redaction. we'll demo a sample later.
[08:20] Anika Sharma: let's see an example for Optimize.
[08:23] Priya Nair: (switching tabs) Optimize shows heatmaps of token retention, routes ranked by sensitive token frequency, and cost impact of retention windows. For payments/charge route we see high sensitive-token frequency — Optimize suggests lowering retention to 0 or tokenization for 7 days.
[08:39] Derek Holt: how do I trust the heatmap? where is data coming from?
[08:43] Priya Nair: it's derived from sampled telemetry — by default we sample 1% of traffic for full-text analysis with redaction applied in-situ; you can increase sample rate for more coverage. sampling respects route-level storage toggles.
[08:55] Anika Sharma: do you ever send samples to Redwood for analysis?
[08:58] Priya Nair: only if you opt in. default is analysis in your tenant. for Hosted customers who opt into Benchmarking we may request sample telemetry but it's anonymized and requires explicit consent.
[09:10] Lena Park: okay. I'd like us to run a bench in staging with our payloads. can we do that?
[09:14] Jordan Lee: absolutely — Derek can share sanitized payloads and we'll run a retention & latency bench. Priya will run it and we'll share the report.
[09:22] Derek Holt: fine. one more Q: are logs redactable retroactively? say we discovered a leak from last month and want to purge persisted data.
[09:29] Priya Nair: yes, we provide bulk deletion tools for persisted records keyed by route/time range. For Hosted customers we can run a purge job and provide a signed manifest. For Private, you can run purge tool locally. note that if you've exported logs off-platform we don't control those.
[09:44] Anika Sharma: can we also lock configs so devs can't flip persistent on in dev?
[09:48] Priya Nair: yes, Org Policies allow enforcement. you can set RBAC so only security or infra roles can change retention.
[09:55] [10:00] Marco Gutierrez: quick demo of API flow when store_requests is toggled mid-run: we keep request data for just-in-time debugging in a ephemeral bucket and then the retention job triggers. Here's an example of how a retention job looks in audit.
[10:15] [10:20] Derek Holt: tiny nit — you mentioned syslog export for audit logs. we prefer journald/elastic. supported?
[10:24] Priya Nair: we support syslog, S3, Kafka, and direct SIEM connectors; elastic is supported via our Kafka/S3 connector. we can show an example mapping.
[10:35] Lena Park: what about legal / procurement asks — DPA, data residency?
[10:39] Jordan Lee: we have a DPA template and region controls — data can be pinned to specific regions. we'll share the DPA and our data flow diagrams.
[10:47] Anika Sharma: show me the security doc link in chat please.
[10:50] [chat paste: link to security pack: https://redwood.example.com/security/pacifictrust-pack]
[10:55] Derek Holt: can we talk about cost — persistent storage obviously costs money. any guidance?
[11:00] Priya Nair: yes, Optimize shows cost per token-day for storage and suggests shorter windows for high-volume routes. We also offer reserved capacity/discounts for Dedicated if you need sustained retention for debugging.
[11:12] Derek Holt: if we go Dedicated is there any difference in retention features?
[11:15] Jordan Lee: feature parity — same Console & API controls; Dedicated just gives you isolated capacity and the option to keep everything in your VPC.
[11:24] Anika Sharma: final question: do you integrate with our internal KMS for key rotation audits?
[11:29] Priya Nair: yes, we log key usage and can surface rotation events to your KMS audit stream. key access is enforced via IAM roles.
[11:38] Lena Park: Ok those are my main things. thanks.
[11:41] Jordan Lee: great, quick recap and next steps — priya will send SOC2 and KMS docs, derek will share sample payloads, i'll draft pilot config and pricing, and we'll schedule the bench. Anything else?
[11:52] Anika Sharma: please include the irreversible vs reversible options clearly in the doc, our compliance team needs that spelled out.
[11:58] Jordan Lee: will do. thanks everyone, we'll follow up by end of week.
[12:02] (call ends)
